extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders in administrative rulemaking and ACUS participants (consultants, committee members, Council/Assembly members, administrative law practitioners, and the public interested in ACUS processes)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive steps ACUS follows to produce Recommendations or Statements: selecting/staffing studies, drafting comprehensive research reports with proposed recommendations, committee review and drafting, Council/Assembly approval, and implementation. Also describes the alternative product 'Statements.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function / Purpose of Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the overarching goal for Recommendations: identify and propose improvements to administrative/regulatory procedures through collaboration between public and private sectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants (authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: consultant engagements must be approved by the Council and are the typical mechanism to initiate studies of processes needing improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of comprehensive research report
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliverable requirement: the study should result in a comprehensive research report that proposes specific recommendations; may be produced by outside consultants or in-house staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and drafting of Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review workflow: committee-level deliberation transforms the research report into a draft Recommendation, which must be forwarded to the Council for approval before submission to the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly adoption and implementation commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, which ACUS undertakes to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalization and follow-through: after Assembly debate and adoption, ACUS commits to implementing the adopted Recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements as an alternative product
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject. ACUS statements are typically the product of the same process that leads to recommendations, but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative output: Statements follow the same procedural pathway but are used to present issues, study conclusions, or comments instead of formal recommendations; ACUS has adopted 20 such statements, and they are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
